COMMERCIAL BOOKKEEPING ACT — CONSOLIDATED TEXT

Part I — General Provisions

Article 1. Scope of Application
This Act applies to all natural and legal persons engaged in commercial bookkeeping
activities within the jurisdiction, including sole traders, partnerships, limited
liability companies, and public companies. Compliance with this Act is mandatory and
non-derogable except where explicitly provided herein.

Article 2. Definitions
For the purposes of this Act, the following definitions apply:
(a) "Client funds" means any monetary assets received by a bookkeeping firm on behalf
of or for the account of a client, regardless of the form in which such assets are
received or held.
(b) "Fee" means any remuneration, commission, charge, or other consideration payable
to a bookkeeping firm in exchange for services rendered.
(c) "Disclosure" means the written communication of material information to a client
in plain language prior to the relevant transaction or service engagement.
(d) "Retention" means the act of holding client funds beyond the period required for
the completion of the instructed transaction.

Article 3. Prohibition on Undisclosed Fees
3.1 No bookkeeping firm shall charge, deduct, or retain any fee from client funds
unless such fee has been explicitly disclosed to the client in writing prior to the
commencement of the relevant service.
3.2 Written disclosure under Article 3.1 must include: (a) the exact amount or
percentage of the fee; (b) the basis for calculation; (c) the timing of deduction;
and (d) the account from which the fee will be deducted.
3.3 Verbal disclosure does not satisfy the requirement of Article 3.1.
3.4 Any fee charged in violation of Article 3.1 must be refunded to the client within
five business days of the client's written demand.

Article 4. Client Fund Segregation
4.1 Client funds must be held in accounts separate from the operating accounts of the
bookkeeping firm at all times.
4.2 No bookkeeping firm shall commingle client funds with its own funds or with the
funds of any other client without the express written consent of all affected clients.
4.3 Client fund accounts must be clearly labelled as such and must be identifiable
in the firm's books as client fund accounts.

Article 5. Record-Keeping Requirements
5.1 Every bookkeeping firm shall maintain accurate and complete records of all
transactions involving client funds for a minimum period of seven years from the
date of the transaction.
5.2 Records must include: (a) the identity of the client; (b) the amount received;
(c) the date of receipt; (d) the purpose of the funds; (e) any fees deducted with
reference to the applicable disclosure document; and (f) the date of return or
disbursement of funds.
5.3 Records must be made available to the relevant supervisory authority within
three business days of a written request.

Article 6. Reporting Obligations
6.1 Bookkeeping firms handling client funds in excess of EUR 10,000 per transaction
must file a transaction report with the Financial Supervision Authority within two
business days of the transaction.
6.2 Suspicious transactions must be reported regardless of amount within 24 hours
of the firm becoming aware of the suspicious circumstances.
6.3 A transaction is suspicious if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the
funds are connected to money laundering, tax evasion, or other financial crime.

Part II — Client Rights

Article 7. Right to Information
7.1 Clients are entitled to receive, upon request, a complete itemised statement of
all fees charged and all transactions conducted on their behalf within the preceding
twelve months.
7.2 Such statements must be provided free of charge within five business days of
the client's written request.
7.3 Bookkeeping firms may not impose conditions on the exercise of rights under
this Article.

Article 8. Right to Refund
8.1 Where a bookkeeping firm has charged fees in excess of those disclosed, the
client is entitled to a full refund of the excess amount plus interest at the
statutory rate from the date of the overcharge.
8.2 The client's right to refund under this Article is not subject to any limitation
period shorter than three years from the date on which the client became aware or
should reasonably have become aware of the overcharge.

Part III — Enforcement

Article 9. Supervisory Authority
9.1 The Financial Supervision Authority is responsible for the supervision and
enforcement of this Act.
9.2 The Authority may conduct inspections, request documents, and impose
administrative sanctions in accordance with the procedures set out in this Part.

Article 10. Administrative Sanctions
10.1 Violations of Articles 3, 4, or 5 are subject to an administrative fine of
not less than EUR 5,000 and not more than EUR 500,000 per violation.
10.2 Repeated violations within a three-year period are subject to a fine of up to
EUR 2,000,000 and may result in revocation of the firm's operating licence.
10.3 The Authority shall publish all final administrative decisions imposing fines
in excess of EUR 50,000 on its official website within thirty days of the decision
becoming final.
